::::{#exm-effective-degrees-of-freedom}
#### Effective degrees of freedom of the three-point fit

In @exm-penalized-least-squares,
the smoother matrix has entries

$$
\ba
(\mat{S}_\l)_{ij}
&= \sbmat{1 & x_i} \sbmat{1/3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1/(2 + \l)} \sbmat{1 \\ x_j}
&& \text{(row } i \text{ of } \mat{B}\text{, then column } j \text{ of } \tp{\mat{B}}\text{)}
\\ &= \frac{1}{3} + \frac{x_i x_j}{2 + \l}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$

so its trace is

$$
\ba
\text{EDF}(\l)
&= \sum_{i=1}^3 \paren{\frac{1}{3} + \frac{x_i^2}{2 + \l}}
&& \text{(sum the diagonal entries)}
\\ &= 1 + \frac{\sum_{i=1}^3 x_i^2}{2 + \l}
&& \text{(sum each term separately)}
\\ &= 1 + \frac{2}{2 + \l}
&& \text{(} \textstyle\sum x_i^2 = 2\text{)}
\ea
$$

- With $\l = 0$, $\text{EDF} = 2$: an unpenalized line has two parameters.
- With $\l = 2$, $\text{EDF} = 1.5$: the penalized slope counts as half a parameter.
- As $\l \to \infty$, $\text{EDF} \to 1$: only the intercept remains.
::::
